properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 17 at 3:27AM CDT until October 17 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE TODAY...

.A cold front is introducing some very dry air with RH values
falling into the low to mid 30s along with windy conditions with
some gusts well into the 30 mph range. Winds are expected to
continue in the mid 20 mph range today. The combination of gusty
winds, current drought conditions, ample dry fuel, and very dry
conditions will allow any fire that develops to spread quickly. A
Red Flag Warnings will continue for a large portion of the area
today. This headline will drop by Sunday, but only the wind speeds
will cause this change. The dry, breezy conditions will remain
causing favorable conditions for fire spread.

* AFFECTED AREA...Pointe Coupee, West Feliciana, East Feliciana,
St. Helena, Washington, Iberville, West Baton Rouge, East
Baton Rouge, Assumption, St. James, Wilkinson, Amite, Pike,
Northern Tangipahoa, Walthall, Southeast St. Tammany, Pearl
River, Northern St. Tammany, Southwestern St. Tammany,
Hancock, Central Tangipahoa, Harrison, Lower Tangipahoa,
Jackson, Northern Livingston, Southern Livingston, Western
Ascension and Eastern Ascension.

* WINDS...North 15 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 16 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
increased fine particle pollution from wildfire smoke.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the areas of San Clemente, Dana Point, San Juan
Capistrano, and Laguna Niguel. Levels of particle pollution can
vary by time and location depending on fire activity and local
weather conditions.

* WHEN...from 4 PM Friday to 10 AM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Particles in wildfire smoke can get deep into the lungs
and cause serious health problems such as heart attacks, strokes,
asthma attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected,
but people with lung or heart disease, older adults, people who are
pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot of time outdoors are
at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, if you smell or see smoke:

* Remain indoors with windows and doors closed
* Avoid intense outdoor physical activity
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* If you must be outdoors, keep the time brief and wear a well-
fitting N-95 mask
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

For the latest air quality forecasts and information, visit the
website at aqmd.gov.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
